clue.text: Reserve determined to join A-Team

parts.note: someone set on a course is determined
read as A and Team, with a side being a team in sport

explanation.surface: A recruit, resolved to sign up with the A-Team, is held back in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A-Team' looks like the TV show, but it splits into A plus SIDE, a team.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something by for later is to keep it in reserve, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Sporty student, depressed

definitions.meaning: at Oxford or Cambridge a student who represents the university at sport is awarded a ...

explanation.surface: A student athlete is feeling low.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxbridge sporting honour gives the student the title, and feeling down is a common colour idiom.

clue.text: Item of furniture, one installed by worker in the home

indicators.note: one thing installed by another is put inside it, so the numeral goes within the worker

parts.note: a char, or charwoman, is a British house cleaner
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A domestic help fits a piece of furniture in someone's house.
explanation.walkthrough: A CHAR is an old British word for a woman paid to clean houses.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat for one person is a basic piece of household furniture.

clue.text: A few words you might say for 'fights'

indicators.note: signals that the word must be spoken, sounding like another

parts.note: a phrase is a short group of words

explanation.surface: Someone offers a brief expression meaning brawls.
explanation.definitionFit: Affrays are public brawls, disturbances of the peace, so they are fights.

clue.text: Secret society getting building work for nothing?

parts.note: something given for nothing is free
masonry is stonework done by builders

explanation.surface: A clandestine fraternity gets its construction jobs done at no charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark nods to the order's origins in stonemasons' guilds.
explanation.definitionFit: The Masons are a fraternal order famous for their secret rituals and handshakes.

clue.text: Finally, sort of junction can be located on map

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece located on another comes after it

parts.note: an atlas is a book of maps
a T-junction is where one road meets another at right angles

explanation.surface: At the end, someone notes a road junction can be found on the map.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverbial phrase meaning eventually, after a long wait.

clue.text: Various people taking the plunge

definitions.meaning: an old-fashioned adjective meaning several or sundry

explanation.surface: A mixed group of folk jump into the water.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic adjective means sundry, and the plural noun means those who plunge headfirst into water.

clue.text: Release 1970s film

definitions.meaning: a 1972 thriller directed by John Boorman

explanation.surface: A movie from the seventies is being released.
explanation.definitionFit: Freeing someone is a rescue, and Boorman's 1972 canoe thriller carries that title.

clue.text: Unfavourable publicity accompanying poet's output

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a piece of publicity
a poet writes verse

explanation.surface: A poet's work comes with bad press.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse conditions are unfavourable or harmful, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Note bachelor always getting repulsed

indicators.note: being driven back, so the word for always is turned around

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful

explanation.surface: A single man keeps being rebuffed when he writes a note.
explanation.definitionFit: A breve is a long musical note, worth two whole notes.

clue.text: On back street of Paris you'll find round coin

indicators.note: the French street name is read backwards

parts.note: rue is French for street
the letter O is round in shape

explanation.surface: On a Parisian back street, someone finds a round coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The currency unit used in France and much of Europe, issued as coins.

clue.text: Stand salted nuts after gym exercises

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the exercises

parts.note: PE is physical education, school gym classes

indicators.note: crazy, so the letters of salted go wild

explanation.surface: Someone eats salty peanuts after a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like the snack being salted, but it signals the anagram of SALTED, giving DESTAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestal is a base or plinth on which a statue stands.

clue.text: Something containing coal for fire

explanation.surface: A coal scuttle to feed the fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A coal merchant's bag holds fuel, and getting the sack means being dismissed.

clue.text: Strangely, after university, learner becomes very sad

indicators.note: the letters of the word after appear in a strange new order

parts.note: L is for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: After going to university, a student becomes very unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' reads as a time link but is the anagram fodder; 'Strangely' turns it into TEARF.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone close to crying is deeply unhappy.

clue.text: One campaigning against closure of cinema showing PC picture?

parts.note: a cinema is also called a screen
an activist trying to save something from closing is a saver

explanation.surface: A campaigner fighting a cinema's closure shows a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A moving image a computer displays when idle, once used to prevent burn-in on monitors.

clue.text: Gosh — weapon is found in river

indicators.note: one piece found in another sits inside it

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
an arm is a weapon, as in firearm

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at a gun discovered in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of surprise or dismay.

clue.text: Attention between start and end of lesson makes you ---

indicators.note: the word for attention is placed between the two outer letters
takes only the first and last letters of lesson

parts.note: to give ear is to listen with attention

explanation.surface: Paying attention from start to finish of a lesson means you pick things up.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the blank: a lesson makes you study and acquire knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson exists to make pupils acquire knowledge, which fills the gap.

clue.text: Writer, for example, is found in centre of Chester

indicators.note: the pieces are found inside the middle letters
takes the central letters of Chester

parts.note: say means for example, as in a fruit, say an apple

explanation.surface: A writer, perhaps, is discovered in central Chester, an English city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' takes EST, the middle three letters of Chester.
explanation.definitionFit: An essayist is an author of short prose pieces, one kind of writer.

clue.text: Cool, quiet Hebridean island featured in story

indicators.note: a thing featured in a story appears inside it

parts.note: a fable is a moral tale
sh is a call for quiet
Iona is an island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland

explanation.surface: A calm Scottish island is the setting of a tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cool in the slang sense is stylish and in vogue.

clue.text: Tough guy organised charades

indicators.note: the letters of charades are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A hard man sets up a parlour game.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard case is slang for a tough, intimidating person.

clue.text: Challenge for climber in severe storm

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words severe storm

explanation.surface: A mountaineer faces a test in a violent storm.
explanation.definitionFit: The world's highest mountain is the ultimate ascent for mountaineers.

clue.text: Don't move wall decoration, we're told

indicators.note: what we hear spoken, so the decorative band sounds like another word

parts.note: a frieze is a decorated band along a wall

explanation.surface: Someone is warned not to disturb a wall ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: The command to stand completely still, as a police officer might shout.

clue.text: Organ used in stage musical, except for the beginning

indicators.note: drop the first letter of the show

parts.note: Oliver! is Lionel Bart's stage musical based on Oliver Twist

explanation.surface: An organ is used in a stage show, apart from the opening.
explanation.definitionFit: A large internal body organ that filters the blood.

clue.text: Count as a hero in Switzerland

definitions.meaning: to count up, as a bank teller tallies money
William, the Swiss folk hero who shot an apple from his son's head

explanation.surface: Someone is reckoned a national hero by the Swiss.
explanation.definitionFit: Counting votes or money is to tally, and William of the apple legend is Switzerland's hero.
